2608.12230.title: Few-Shot Ordinal Learning for Day-Wise Freshness Estimation with Hyperspectral Fish Images
2608.12230.paper_summary: Non-destructive food quality assessment has increasingly benefited from hyperspectral imaging (HSI), which captures spectral signatures linked to biochemical changes during storage. Estimating day-wise freshness, however, remains challenging owing to strong inter-fillet variability and scarce labelled data per product. All existing deep learning approaches for HSI-based freshness prediction operate under full supervision, requiring densely annotated training sets that are costly to obtain at the individual-product level. We introduce, to the best of our knowledge, the first few-shot learning framework for HSI-based food quality estimation. Each fillet defines a distinct episodic task, and a CORAL-style ordinal prediction head captures the ranked nature of freshness progression through cumulative threshold modelling. Biologically grounded monotonicity and embedding smoothness constraints further guide predictions toward plausible trajectories. On a 16-day salmon HSI dataset under a strict unseen-fillet protocol, our method achieves a mean absolute error of 1.58 days and 2-day accuracy of 72.3% with only three labelled days per fillet, substantially outperforming scalar regression and label-distribution baselines under an identical unseen-fillet protocol.
2608.12230.paper_summary_zh: 非破壞性食品品質評估越來越受益於高光譜成像（HSI），該技術捕捉與儲存過程中生化變化相關的光譜特徵。然而，由於魚片之間的變異性強以及每個產品的標記數據稀少，逐日新鮮度的估計仍然具有挑戰性。所有現有的基於HSI的新鮮度預測深度學習方法均在全監督下運行，這需要密集標註的訓練集，而這在單個產品層面上獲得的成本高昂。我們引入了，據我們所知，首個基於HSI的食品品質估計的少量學習框架。每個魚片定義了一個獨特的情節任務，而CORAL風格的序數預測頭則通過累積閾值建模捕捉新鮮度進展的排名特性。生物學基礎的單調性和嵌入平滑性約束進一步引導預測朝向合理的軌跡。在一個為期16天的鮭魚HSI數據集上，根據嚴格的未見魚片協議，我們的方法達到了1.58天的平均絕對誤差和72.3%的2天準確率，僅需每個魚片三天的標記數據，顯著超越了在相同未見魚片協議下的標量回歸和標籤分佈基準。
